newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's premier says no-confidence move will fail.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's premier says no-confidence move will fail.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, facing a communist backed no-confidence motion, said on Tuesday he was confident of victory despite the desertion of key supporters in parliament.

"I am going to face (the motion) courageously since they (the opposition) don't have any substantial charge against me," Deuba told foreign media reporters at his office. "I am confident that they will not get the required majority."
Nepal's state radio said King Birendra had summoned parliament for a special session on December 16 to take up the no-confidence motion, on which voting would be held later.

To topple Deuba, his opponents would need at least 103 votes in the 205-seat House of Representatives. Nepal's constitution requires the motion to be passed by a majority of the members of the house whose current strength is only 200.
On Sunday, 11 breakaway deputies of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), holding the balance of power, announced they were withdrawing support for Deuba's 15-month-old coalition.
Seven of 13 RPP ministers resigned from Deuba's 46-member centre-right government.
The RPP faction accused Deuba of harassing its activists and breaking an unspecified pledge to the coalition partners.
The three-party coalition controls 108 seats in the 205-seat lower house, where Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party has 86 lawmakers.
The RPP, considered close to the monarchy, has 19 seats and the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP) has three members.
But the opposition United-Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, with 87 deputies, has joined the 11 RPP rebels and had asked the king to convene parliament to take up the motion against Deuba.

The communists and rebel RPP faction claimed they control at least 102 votes and would win over more deputies. "We are fully confident that the motion will be passed by more than 103 votes," UML general secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal told Reuters.
UML officials said a no-confidence motion would be formally registered at the parliament secretariat on Wednesday. A vote on the motion cannot be held until at least 10 days afterwards.
The UML and RPP rebels have the support of two independents and two NSP members. The NSP disputes that claim.
Political analysts said the three deputies from the leftist Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party (NWPP) could settle Deuba's fate. The NWPP has in the past not voted with the UML.
In March, six RPP ministers resigned from the administration, but they patched up their differences with the government in time for Deuba to survive a no-confidence motion.
